text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Payment of June pensions will start on Thursday, but only in the Sarajevo canton, due to a lack of funds in the Bosnian pension agency, officials said.
- The main Bosnian trade union requests that the lowest pension in the Moslem-Croat federation, which is now equivalent to 60 German marks, be doubled.
- The federation government is due to discuss amendments to the draft customs law as well as possible limits on retail prices of cigarettes and other tobacco products.
- U.S. diplomat Robert Beecroft says formation of joint police in the Mostar area will be completed by next Monday at the latest.
- Chairman of the European Commission mission to Bosnia, Donato Kerini, said the donors' conference will be held in Brussels this month with or without representatives from the country's Serb entity.
- If the Bosnian Serb side fails to attend the fund-raising conference, the Serb entity will receive support only for humanitarian projects, Kerini said.
- Italy's transport trade union donated 360,000 German marks ($210,000 dollars) for reconstruction of the railroad training center in Sarajevo.

- The Social Democratic Party says it will boycott the September local elections unless the Organisation for Security and Cooperation (OSCE) mission checks the validity of registration documents in the disputed town of Brcko.
- Officials of the U.S. Agency for International Development and mayors of four central Bosnian municipalities signed on Wednesday a memorandum worth $1.6 million for electrical power projects.
- The Bosnian railway company can afford to run only transport trains on the route linking Sarajevo to the Adriatic port of Ploce. Launching passenger train service will depend on foreign donations.
- First-year students at universities in the Moslem-Croat federation will not have to pay tuition fees, says the federation minister of education, science, culture and sports, Fahrudin Rizvanbegovic.
- Two Frenchmen accused of robbery and murder were sentenced to twenty years each in a Zenica court.
- Acting president of the Serb Democratic Party, Aleksa Buha, accused Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic of "asking for a international protectorate over institutions in the Serb entity".

- The first private brewery in Bosnia opened in Sarajevo's suburb of Ilidza on Wednesday. The brewery, using hops from the Czech Republic and Slovenia, will produce a lager and a dark ale and will employ 20 workers initially.
- The international supervisor for Brcko approved for the first time the return of 500 Moslem families to the central district of Brcko. --Sarajevo Newsroom, +387-71-663-864
